title: Fasten a bra’s back hooks on a torso form
instruction: Fasten both back hooks of the bra in the outermost eye row and leave the band untwisted and securely closed on the torso form.
context: Fastening a bra requires holding two elastic fabric ends under tension while engaging small ungated hooks. This task isolates that part of dressing assistance.
setup: A rigid dressmaker’s bust manikin with an oval band-line cross-section (260 mm side to side × 160 mm front to back, measured 155 mm above the tabletop) wears a prepared Simplicity 8711 size-32A bra fitted with a BraBuilders Mini 2 Hook closure (32 mm high, three eye rows, nominally 55–56 mm closed width), two ordinary underside hooks engaging recessed eyes with overlapping tapes. The non-working garment is supported on the form; the two working wings each have an unloaded span of 83 ± 2 mm from the fixed wing anchor to the tape seam, with the loose tape centres 80 ± 2 mm apart. Hook spacing is 16 mm and wire diameter 0.8 mm. Both arms use 40 x 6 x 1 mm finger extensions with a 4 N jaw limit. Fixed dimensions and layout are in the README and geometry.py.
scoring: Score the final state. Zero for damage, any wing exceeding 1.6 times its rest span, a twisted wing or insufficient release. With both open hands at least 55 mm clear for the final 3 seconds: 0.5 if at least one hook remains in its outer-row eye throughout; 1.0 if both do. Highest qualifying tier applies. Grasping or bringing the ends together earns no credit.
fidelity: Native elastic end links represent the working wings; the non-working garment is supported on the form. Intermediate ribbons are visual: distributed cloth contact and wrinkles are omitted. Reinforced tapes, hooks and eyes have native collision, with no auto-latch. Contact-checked finite finger joints approximate pinch friction. Elastic overload, twist, slip and failed retention lose credit.
reset_notes: Unhook both hooks, restore the two loose ends and inspect the elastic wings and closure. Replace any damaged garment before resetting. Fixed layout; no object jitter.
